target_customer: Pharmaceutical and clinical partners developing cancer therapeutics; first program aimed at pediatric liver cancer with Texas Children's Hospital
problem: Natural oncolytic viruses are expensive and error prone to manipulate. The company engineers synthetic RNA viruses with selective infection and replication to kill cancer cells while sparing healthy ones.
business_model: Preclinical biotech developing oncolytic viral therapeutics, with value expected from licensing or clinical-stage milestones
product_category: Synthetic biology, oncolytic virus cancer therapeutics

founders.name: Peter Weijmarshausen
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page, which describes him as a serial entrepreneur who led software and product teams at three companies.

founders.name: Chad Moles
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked in biotech and in academic and public health settings at Columbia and Tulane. 2048 Ventures calls him Chief Science Officer. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing synthetic RNA oncolytic viruses with an on-switch for selective replication, manufacturing them to clinical grade and proving efficacy and safety is research-grade work that needs animal data and regulatory clearance.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary virus designs and any future clinical data are hard to copy, but the oncolytic field has many funded players and the platform remains preclinical.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move against the company found. A 2025 manufacturing agreement with Genezen was announced instead.

market_need_then: Pediatric hepatoblastoma has few targeted options, and 2048 Ventures argued in January 2020 that advances in synthetic biology made engineered viruses better than manipulated natural ones, which it called expensive and error prone.

branding.domain_note: Uses humanegenomics.com with an added letter e, not the exact words; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; the YC copy uses a '2 factor authentication' analogy for selective infection and replication.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself beyond a 2021 trade article headline about 3D-printing viruses; name pairs a warm adjective with genomics but is not distinctive.

outcome_analysis: Humane Genomics remains active and preclinical. It raised a small pre-seed in early 2020, joined YC in summer 2021, and announced a seed led by Union Square Ventures in February 2025 with the amount undisclosed. In November 2025 it announced a cGMP manufacturing partnership with Genezen and moved labs to Alexandria LaunchLabs. No clinical trial was found, so the outcome is still open and the long gap between rounds suggests slow, capital-constrained progress.
notes: The Fierce Biotech article (Aug 27, 2021) and finsmes page returned 403, so the 2025 seed rests on search result summaries from several aggregators; amount undisclosed there, while one aggregator cites $8.12M total and another $4M, both unverified. An aggregator claims $125k from YC, unverified and not recorded. Andrew Hessel appears in the 2048 post as part of the team but is not stated as a co-founder, so he is not listed. Competitor list left empty: oncolytic virus peers such as Replimune, Candel and Turnstone surfaced only in undated search summaries, so no dated source was available. Founding year 2019 per YC; other sources say 2020.
